newsitem.title: SWEDEN: POLL-INCENTIVE H1 PROFIT SEEN 11.7 BLN SKR.
newsitem.headline: POLL-INCENTIVE H1 PROFIT SEEN 11.7 BLN SKR.

text.p: Swedish medical technology and investment group Incentive was expected to post a profit after financial items of 11.70 billion crowns for the first half of 1997, a Reuters poll of nine analysts found on Wednesday.
The profit will include a capital gain of 11.20 billion crowns realised as Incentive sold off its holdings in various companies to focus on its medical technology business.
This consists of 9.90 billion crowns for ABB shares, 435 million crowns for Electrolux, 800 million crowns for TA Hydronics and 65 million crowns for Wabco.
Estimates varied between 11.33 and 11.94 billion crowns.
"It is hard to estimate after everything that Incentive has done. It will be interesting to see how Gambro is going," said one analyst.
The profit after financial items for the first half of 1996 was 1.99 billion crowns.
For full year 1997 analysts estimated a profit after financial items including capital gains of 12.68 billion crowns.
Analysts interviewed for the poll were from Aros, Enskilda, Fischer Partners, Handelsbanken, James Capel, Kleinwort Benson, Myrberg & Wiklund, Nordbanken, Paribas, Swedbank.
Incentive's half year report is due out on August 11.
